title: Relapse versus reinfection as a genomic fork
dek: A late isolate sitting a handful of SNPs from the baseline genome looks like relapse or persistence. A distant, often different-lineage pair looks like reinfection or mixed infection. Thresholds are screens, not likelihoods.
story: Recurrent TB after treatment is two different scientific objects. Relapse (or persistence) is the same strain returning — residual bacilli, often from a poorly sterilised lesion, sometimes with acquired resistance. Reinfection is a new strain, common in high-incidence settings and in HIV, and a reason that “cure” at six months is not lifelong immunity.

WGS made the fork operational: a pairwise SNP distance, a tree, sometimes mixed-allele fractions. Near-identity (after a stated mask) supports relapse. A different lineage, or a large distance within a lineage, supports reinfection. Heteroresistance and mixed infection sit in the middle and can fool a single colony pick.

Epidemiology still has to speak. A 2-SNP pair six years later can be relapse with a slow clock, or a common source still circulating. A 80-SNP pair in two weeks is mixed infection or a sample swap until proven otherwise. The transmission-genomics stats plate is the caveat engine; this plate is the clinical fork.
deep: State the mask (PE/PPE, repeats, optionally DR genes), the reference, and the clock you believe. Unmasked PE_PGRS distances are not this fork.

Acquired resistance on a near-identical background is a relapse-plus-evolution story (cavity under pressure). A new rpoB on a different lineage is reinfection with RR-TB, not “the first course created S450L in a new clade overnight.”
HIV and high force of infection raise the prior on reinfection. Low-incidence settings raise the prior on relapse. Bayes lives here as a prior, not as a p-value.
Culture contamination and swapped tubes mimic both forks. Discordant NTM or a second patient’s barcode is a lab incident.

visual.caption: Recurrent isolate in, then a genomic comparison. Near-identity heads to relapse/persistence; a distant or different-lineage genome heads to reinfection. Mixed BAM or sample-swap is the decision node you must not skip.

example.title: Month-18 isolate, 3 SNPs, new gyrA
example.setup: Baseline DS-TB, L4, treated with HRZE. Recurrence at month 18. WGS: same barcode, 3 SNPs after a standard core mask, plus gyrA D94G at AF 0.95. The patient lives in a high-incidence city.

steps.title: Same strain plus evolution
steps.body: 3 SNPs and a shared barcode is a relapse/persistence picture, not a new L2 reinfection. D94G on that background is acquired FQ-R (or unmasking of a minority) under pressure if a FQ was used — check the history.

steps.title: Do not over-call reinfection because incidence is high
steps.body: A high prior on reinfection does not beat a 3-SNP identity. Reinfection would look like a different lineage or a long distance.

steps.title: Lesion hygiene
steps.body: Ask about the original cavity, adherence, and whether FQ-containing regimens were given. The genome forked to relapse-plus-resistance, not to a new contact’s strain.

example.takeaway: Near-identity is relapse/persistence until a mixed BAM says otherwise. Distance is reinfection.

check.prompt: A recurrent isolate with the same lineage barcode and 2 core SNPs from baseline most strongly supports:
choices: Relapse or persistence of the same strain (or a missed mixed infection if the BAM is mixed)
Reinfection with a typical between-lineage distance
check.answer: Relapse or persistence of the same strain (or a missed mixed infection if the BAM is mixed)
check.why: Near-identity is the relapse fork. Mixed infection is the caveat, not the default.

check.prompt: Baseline L4; recurrence L2, ~250 SNPs. The working call is:
choices: Relapse with a fast clock of 250 SNPs in 4 months
Reinfection (or mixed infection / swap until the lab is clean)
check.answer: Reinfection (or mixed infection / swap until the lab is clean)
check.why: Different major lineage is not a 6-month clock. Check swaps, then treat as new infection.

whyWrong.BCG bladder therapy: RD1/BCG story, not L2 pulmonary recurrence by default.

check.prompt: On the flow map, why is a mixed/swap node drawn beside near versus far?
choices: Because sample mix-ups and mixed infection can mimic either fork if you only look at a consensus FASTA
check.answer: Because sample mix-ups and mixed infection can mimic either fork if you only look at a consensus FASTA
check.why: A consensus sequence hides 40/60 lineage splits. Look at the BAM.

whyWrong.Because Xpert measures SNP distance: Xpert interrogates RRDR, not a core alignment.
